deviations_recorded_before_measurement.frozen_text: The wrapper opens an interval scope when `values` returns on a conv-QKV layer and closes it at the next provider entry.
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.code_fact: Both call sites copy KEYS before VALUES are requested: exec/mod.rs:1441-1442 (`provider.keys(l).to_vec()` then `provider.values(l).to_vec()`) and exec/decode.rs:821-822 (the same order through `self.kv.state()`). The key copy therefore happens between `keys` returning and `values` being entered — outside the frozen interval.
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.consequence_if_followed_literally: the frozen interval sees only the value copy: h row-sized allocations, not the 2·h M4 forecasts. M4 would read FALSIFIED by the instrument's placement, not by the code.
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.deviation: the interval is the UNION of two executor-only windows on a conv-QKV layer: `keys` return → next provider entry, and `values` return → next provider entry. Neither window contains provider code. Both the frozen window alone (values-return only) and the union are reported; M4 is adjudicated on the union, and the frozen-window count is recorded beside it so the deviation's effect is visible (expected: exactly h in the frozen window, 2·h in the union).
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.why_this_is_not_a_forecast_edit: the quantity M4 forecasts (the executor's copy of every held K and V row) is unchanged; only the instrument's window is corrected to contain it.

deviations_recorded_before_measurement.frozen_text: the perturbation sized to the row's own scale (a ULP of a large cell, never of zero)
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.operationalisation: perturb the largest-magnitude cell c of the chosen K row AND of the chosen V row to c·(1 + 2⁻⁴). Scale-relative and never applied to a zero cell; large enough that an in-range dependence cannot round away. Recorded here because 'a ULP' could be read as one unit in the last place, which an in-range softmax can legitimately absorb without a bit change — that reading would manufacture a false 'no dependence' in the in-range direction.

ndarray exposes no capacity for an owned Array2. The matrix's allocated bytes are read from the measuring allocator's live-allocation table, keyed by the matrix's data pointer (`KvCache.layers[l]` → `as_ptr()`); every allocation made inside a provider scope is entered in that table with its size, and removed on free wherever the free happens. A matrix pointer absent from the table is an instrument failure, never a zero.

events inside an append scope are classified by POINTER IDENTITY against the provider's storage after the call (matrix data pointers, the last view row's pointer, the outer Vec pointers), not by size alone. On the fixtures a row is 16 bytes and the smallest outer-Vec header allocation is 96 bytes = 6 rows, so size classification would collide.

deviations_recorded_before_measurement.instrument: I6 storage identity through a type-erased handoff
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.operationalisation:
a ContinuationHandoff holds `Box`, so the canonical matrix is unreachable from the test through the trait. The handoff is built from a test factory whose provider is `Measured

`; the wrapper holds a shared inventory sink and writes its backing inventory (pointer and capacity of every row, matrix, latent row and recurrent buffer) into it when a flag is set, on its next `set_position(p)` call (the test re-sets the current position through `state_mut()`, a no-op for every provider; `&mut` is needed because recurrent buffers are reachable only through `recurrent_state(&mut self)`). The inventory is taken outside every measured scope.

deviations_recorded_before_measurement.instrument: I1_thread_integrity applied to the M8 recurrent-operator window
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.recorded: after the first oute-mamba2attn-250m run (ProductionBackend, harness a097c9c5), BEFORE any M8 copy measurement is adjudicated
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.fact: ProductionBackend partitions projections across worker threads, so every recurrent window that spans an operator saw foreign-thread allocations (10,319 on row/v1). Under the frozen rule those windows are INVALID; the only integrity-clean windows on that run are empty ones (recurrent_state followed directly by another provider call).
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.what_the_invalid_windows_showed_on_the_o: exactly one conv-history-sized allocation per Mamba2 (36,864 B) and per conv-QKV (98,304 B) call. Recorded, NOT adjudicated: owner-thread counts are what the integrity rule exists to distrust.
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.operationalisation: M8's per-call copy clause is adjudicated only from windows with zero foreign allocations. Those come from the serial ReferenceBackend (CpuParallelism::Serial semantics — 'the reference oracle'), on oute-mamba2attn-250m (Mamba2 + conv-QKV) and on the in-tree fixtures: the KDA+MLA hybrid (KDA) and hybrid_lllf_f32_model (Gated DeltaNet), which is pub and was not listed in the freeze's subjects. M8's payload and n-independence clauses are storage facts from provider scopes (integrity-clean on every run) and are adjudicated on the ProductionBackend runs as frozen.
deviations_recorded_before_measurement.why_not_a_forecast_edit: backend choice is not fixed by the freeze; the rule that a window with foreign allocations is INVALID is kept, not relaxed

records.shas: qwen3-0.6b and oute (production) at a097c9c5; every other record at 0924df88. The only harness change between them adds the D6 tests (gated-delta fixture, oute on the reference backend); no instrument code changed. The fixture and D6 records ran with those two tests in the working tree, committed with this record.
subjects_run: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct.s7.vindex3 (24 positions; peak RSS 28 GiB, weights mapped)
records.controls: all pass: negative (no scope → 0 attributed), recorder silence (empty scope → 0), positive (a 33-float Vec is seen with its size and table entry), thread integrity (a planted worker-thread allocation is foreign), realloc classification (moved ⇔ pointer changed; moved bytes = old sizes), parity (row/v1 ≡ canonical/v1 bit-for-bit on all 9 subjects). All 18 subject×provider runs instrument-valid: 0 foreign allocations in provider scopes, 0 unresolved capacities, 0 unclassified append events, no dropped events, live table never overflowed.
instrument_artifacts: The ~16 MB 'seal' scope in the M6 record is Measured's own preallocated call-record buffer (1<<16 records), built by the test factory inside begin(); it is the instrument, not the provider.

Operator-spanning recurrent windows on ProductionBackend and on the reference backend's batched prefill contain worker-thread allocations; per D6 they are INVALID and their owner-thread counts are recorded but not adjudicated.

Realloc moved-vs-in-place is heap-layout dependent and varies run to run: a re-run of the fixtures after a behaviour-neutral refactor (Window variant rename, clippy) reproduced every record field except canonical's matrix_realloc_moved / _in_place counts in one prefill phase (sliding 10→7 moves, 352→176 B; gated-delta 4→5, 512→768 B). M2's bound (moved ≤ 2× final matrix) holds in both runs; realloc-move magnitudes are therefore stated as observed values, not constants.

M1.observed: 2.000–2.862 on every subject and phase with K/V rows (fixtures 2.0–2.78; qwen 2.0–2.6; oute 2.0–2.6; gemma 2.822–2.862). N/A on kda-mla and Kimi (no ordinary K/V rows), per applies_when.
M1.note: 2.0 exactly occurs where the matrix's capacity equals its rows (a growth step landed on the count); the forecast's lower bound is reached, not crossed.

M2.observed: row/v1: 0 row-sized allocations and the stored row IS the moved-in row on all 43,690 appends across subjects. canonical/v1: exactly 2 duplicate (view) allocations per append, matrix rows +1 per append, and realloc-move traffic ≤ 2× final matrix bytes everywhere (gemma 284.4 MB moved vs 570.4 MB final matrix; qwen 44.8 vs 58.7 MB).
M2.instrument_note: raw row-sized counts also include each matrix's first one-row allocation; pointer identity (D4) separates them — e.g. dense 36 row-sized = 32 views + 4 matrix first allocations.

M3.observed: keys lends every held row (h) and the step covers h+1 positions; selected range = min(h+1, w). gemma: 29 sliding layers, at end n=1,124, w=1,024, held-outside fraction 0.089 = 1 − 1024/1124. I2 holds in both directions on all 29 gemma sliding layers (row 0 perturbed → logits bit-identical; row 1,115 → changed) and on the fixture (window 3).

M4.observed: every conv-QKV call, production and reference: row-sized allocations = 2·h exactly (76/76 production calls + all reference calls), plus exactly 2 other allocations (the two outer Vecs). The frozen window alone saw exactly h on every call — as D1 predicted; followed literally the freeze would have read FALSIFIED by instrument placement.

M5.observed: hybrid fixture: batched prefill of 6 → 21 kv_b calls = n(n+1)/2; decode steps at h = 6, 7, 8 → 7, 8, 9 = h+1. Shape control: q 32→48 ×9, kv_a 32→20 ×9, kv_b 16→64 ×45 (21+7+8+9); o_proj 32→32 shares its shape with KDA projections and is counted with them.
M5.real_kimi_derived: geometry kv_lora_rank 512, 32 heads × (128 nope + 128 v): each re-derivation is a 512→8,192 projection (4.19 M MAC) producing a fresh 32 KiB Vec, beside a 2 KiB normalised latent and a 256 B rope-K copy (34.25 KiB per re-derived row). 7 MLA layers ⇒ per token at held latent rows h: (h+1)·29.4 M MAC and (h+1)·240 KiB of allocation. At h = 4,096: ≈120 GMAC and ≈1.0 GB allocated per token. DERIVED (count × geometry), not observed on Kimi.
M5.reported_not_adjudicated: the append clone (mla.rs:310): 576 floats = 2,304 B per MLA layer per token.

M6.observed: insert → take → resume is the same 6 allocations / 872 B (sizes 64, 10, 9, 684, 9, 96) on every subject × provider, independent of state size (1.3 KB to 8.4 KB here) and kind (rows, matrices, latent, recurrent); 0 realloc moves; I6: every backing pointer and capacity identical before insert and after resume on all 6 runs.
M6.collision_disclosed: the operationalisation 'continuation-sized = size equal to a backing's capacity' fired on the dense fixture (row = 64 B) against the 64 B allocation present on every subject; the invariant profile identifies it as cache bookkeeping, not a copy.

M7.observed: canonical 0.349–0.500 ⊂ [0.30, 0.52] (gemma 0.349–0.354, qwen/oute 0.385–0.5); row/v1 = 0 exactly. N/A where no K/V rows.

M8.verdict: FALSIFIED (one clause, in the benign direction)

clauses.payload = RecurrentGeometry::bytes(): HELD on all 5 recurrent subjects (Kimi 44,892,160 B; oute 30,785,536 B; fixtures 6,528 / 6,144 B)
clauses.allocated ≥ payload and independent of n: HELD: allocated = payload, constant across batched → resumed → decode on every subject
clauses.per-call copy = the conv-history buffer: HELD for Mamba2 (36,864 B) and conv-QKV (98,304 B): exactly 1 conv-history-sized allocation in all 128 integrity-clean oute decode windows on the reference backend (D6). FALSIFIED for KDA: 0 copies in every integrity-clean window, fixture (9/9) and real Kimi (80/80) — KDA updates its three conv buffers in place. Gated DeltaNet NOT ADJUDICABLE: the fixture's conv history, delta matrix and 256-float activations are all 1,024 B, so signature classification cannot attribute (4 same-sized allocations per clean window).

M8.lesson: the forecast generalised the Mamba2/GatedDelta/conv-QKV transcription (conv history .to_vec() per call) to every recurrent operator; KDA was written differently. The copy is an operator implementation fact, per operator.

ranking.basis: real containers at the measured lengths; resident bytes and per-token traffic ranked separately. Classes: (a) forced by the read contract → VIEW-1; (b) operator implementation → its own perf rung; (c) provider storage choice → provider work.

resident_bytes.item: canonical/v1's Vec<Vec<f32>> views — a full second copy of every K/V row, existing only to lend its matrix authority as &[Vec<f32>]
resident_bytes.magnitude: = K/V payload: gemma 313.1 MB at 1,124 positions; qwen 40.4 MB at 176
resident_bytes.note: canonical/v1 is the SERVER's provider (vindex3.rs:295-304); row/v1 (the CLI default) already matches the contract with zero duplicates

resident_bytes.magnitude: gemma 257.4 MB (570.4 MB capacity for 313.1 MB of rows); qwen 18.4 MB; 0–100% of payload depending on where the growth step lands

resident_bytes.item: rows held outside every sliding window — the contract indexes rows absolutely from position 0, so no provider may drop them
resident_bytes.magnitude: gemma 23.8 MB at 1,124 positions (29 layers × 100 rows × 8 KiB), linear in n − w: ≈1.70 GB at 8,192 positions; held by both providers
resident_bytes.note: WINDOW-1 cannot exist until VIEW-1 removes absolute from-0 indexing

resident_bytes.item: one heap allocation per row per K and V (the Vec in &[Vec<f32>]) and its outer-Vec header
resident_bytes.magnitude: gemma 76,432 row allocations + 3.3 MB headers; small in bytes, large in count
Kimi 44.9 MB, oute 30.8 MB, constant; not avoidable

per_token_traffic.item: MLA re-derives every held latent row through kv_b_proj on every call
per_token_traffic.magnitude: Kimi (derived): (h+1)·29.4 M MAC and (h+1)·240 KiB allocated per token; ≈120 GMAC / ≈1.0 GB at h = 4,096
per_token_traffic.note: the latent-row contract is not the cause; the operator caches nothing it decompresses

per_token_traffic.item: conv-QKV copies every held K and V row per call (mod.rs:1441-1442, decode.rs:821-822)
per_token_traffic.magnitude: oute: 4 layers × 2·h × 8 KiB = 64 KiB·h per token (6.1 MB at h = 95; ≈268 MB at h = 4,096); quadratic over a sequence
per_token_traffic.note: the executor clones to release the &self borrow of keys/values before taking &mut recurrent_state. Either an executor restructure or a VIEW-1 split borrow removes it; decide at the VIEW-1 freeze, do not assume it is VIEW-1's.

per_token_traffic.magnitude: 8·kv_dim B per layer per position: gemma 34 × 8 KiB = 272 KiB per token
gemma 284.4 MB moved over a 1,100-token prefill; amortised, ≤ 2× final matrix

per_token_traffic.item: conv-history .to_vec() per recurrent call (Mamba2, conv-QKV; Gated DeltaNet by code reading; not KDA)

VIEW_1_scope_from_class_a: remove the forced duplicate: let a provider lend rows from its own representation (matrix, contiguous, paged) without materialising Vec<Vec<f32>>
remove absolute from-0 indexing: a view carries its base position, so a provider may hold only the live window (the prerequisite for WINDOW-1)
remove per-row heap granularity as a contract requirement
open question for the freeze, not a commitment: whether VIEW-1 also offers a split borrow (KV view + &mut recurrent) that retires the conv-QKV copy, or whether that is an executor rung
not_VIEW_1: MLA re-derivation → an operator perf rung (cache decompressed k_nope/v, or absorb kv_b into q/o)
canonical matrix growth slack and realloc moves → provider work (or a server default decision: row/v1 already avoids the duplicate and the slack)

deviations_preserved.rule: Listed as recorded above, unchanged. Each changed how something was measured, never what was forecast.
deviations_preserved.D1: conv-QKV interval = union of the keys and values windows. Necessary: the frozen window alone saw exactly h on every call and would have read M4 FALSIFIED by instrument placement; both counts are in the record.
deviations_preserved.D2: I2 perturbation = the largest cell × (1 + 2⁻⁴), K and V both.
deviations_preserved.D3: canonical matrix capacity from the live-allocation table (ndarray exposes none).
deviations_preserved.D4: append traffic classified by pointer identity (fixture row sizes collide with header sizes).
deviations_preserved.D5: storage identity through the type-erased handoff via an inventory sink on the wrapper.
deviations_preserved.D6: M8's copy clause adjudicated only from integrity-clean windows (serial reference backend); ProductionBackend's worker threads make its operator windows INVALID under the kept rule.

corrections_preserved.rule: Mistakes of the executor, caught and corrected before the affected numbers were committed. They are recorded here because the committed record would otherwise look cleaner than the experiment was.

K1_D5_trigger.what: D5 first named `position()` as the inventory trigger; enumerating recurrent buffers needs `&mut self`, which `position(&self)` cannot give. Reworded to `set_position(p)`.
K1_D5_trigger.when: before any measurement; the local commit 1a90f6e5 was amended to 86a29637 before it was pushed

K2_M3_selected_range.what: the M3 metric first computed the kernel's selected range as min(h, w) and n at the end as the last h. `keys` is called BEFORE the position's own row is appended (the fixture step at position 7 is offered 7 rows), so the step covers h + 1 positions: corrected to min(h + 1, w) and n_end = last h + 1.
K2_M3_selected_range.when: found reading the first fixture records; corrected before the harness commit a097c9c5 and before any real subject ran
K2_M3_selected_range.effect: the held-outside fraction on the sliding fixture was 0.7 under the error and 0.727 corrected; I2's witness always used the correct range [position + 1 − w, position], so no I2 verdict changed

K3_M5_kimi_allocation.what: the derived Kimi MLA allocation first counted only kv_b_proj's 32 KiB output per re-derived row (229 KiB·(h+1) per token, ≈940 MB at h = 4,096). Each re-derived row also allocates a 2 KiB normalised latent and a 256 B rope-K copy: 34.25 KiB per row × 7 MLA layers = 240 KiB·(h+1), ≈1.0 GB at h = 4,096.
K3_M5_kimi_allocation.when: found re-deriving every figure before the execution commit; corrected before 6c5ad2ac
K3_M5_kimi_allocation.effect: M5's magnitude (derived, not adjudicated) up by ≈5%; no verdict changed

disclosures_preserved: M6: the size-match operationalisation of 'continuation-sized' fired on the dense fixture (64 B rows) against the 64 B cache-bookkeeping allocation present on every subject; M6 adjudicated HELD on the invariant transfer profile and I6 identity.
Gated DeltaNet M8 copy clause not adjudicable (buffer and activation sizes collide at 1,024 B).
